subject.title: Control UI: migrate composite controls to accessible web components

question: Should Control UI standardize suitable composite controls on Web Awesome Core after the dependency-free accessibility repairs, or keep all composite behavior in repository-owned Lit components?
rationale: Both paths can improve accessibility, but the permanent dependency, visual-theme contract, migration breadth, and future component ownership require explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Phased pilot
options.body: Approve native repairs first, then migrate one representative dialog or tab surface to Web Awesome Core with bundle, theme, keyboard, and assistive-technology proof before broader adoption.

options.title: Native components only
options.body: Keep the dependency surface unchanged and centralize accessible Lit primitives within `ui/src/components`, accepting ongoing ownership of composite-control behavior.

options.title: Approve full migration
options.body: Adopt Web Awesome Core as the preferred composite-control layer and plan the affected Control UI surfaces as a coordinated multi-PR program.

recommendation.title: Phased pilot
recommendation.body: Approve native repairs first, then migrate one representative dialog or tab surface to Web Awesome Core with bundle, theme, keyboard, and assistive-technology proof before broader adoption.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the staged direction and are the clearest available sponsor for the Control UI dependency and rollout choice.
